adit_friend.about: {dock_loader} counts the captain as a friend, and keeps lists for them

first_friend.about: the captain found the first old friend (chapter I ends)

ship_never_came_out.about: {dock_loader}'s lists show the captain's ship never came out of the needle

the_pod.about: a needle threw the captain out; years asleep in a pod until a salvager found it; the ship did not come with them

quiet: The Hansa's old hall at Alpha has a museum wing now. Its queue is shorter than the hiring hall's.
Alpha's ring traffic never stops. The controllers sleep in shifts, and so do the ships.
Beta's farm drums turn overhead, slow as a held breath. Somewhere up there a trading house is burning a surplus.
The cargo ring smells of wet soil from the drums. Even the steel here is a little green.
Lift cages rattle up from the deep levels with a shift's worth of tired faces. Nobody looks at the button for level nine.
Gamma's company store still prints its prices on paper, so nobody can say they changed overnight.
A hovertank skims the test strip past the plant, its skirt hissing on the dust. Then another. Then the first one back.
Geod's Row runs green to the horizon. The land next to it is fenced, and the fence is very well kept.
Epsilon's promenade still flies the banners of a gala nobody remembers. The holograms on them have faded to ghosts of ghosts.
The needle office at Epsilon posts its timetable in three calendars: dock time, ship time and 'other'.

Ancient Ruins Alpha.system: Tau Ceti, in the debris disk

Ancient Ruins Beta.system: Epsilon Indi, a moon of the cold giant Ab

Alien Signal Research Outpost Y.system: Sol, the outer system: a dish pointed at Lyra, past HD 178911

intro.again.text: {origin.name} has been through 2533 once already, as {origin.rank}. The hiring hall at {place} has your face on file under another date. The clerk decides it is a filing error. In a way, it is.

intro.from_cargo2.text: {origin.name} flew the needles of 2460 as {origin.rank}. That was seventy-three years ago by the dock clocks, and a good deal less by yours. The ring you chased is a joke now. The Debacle made it one.

intro.colonel.text: {origin.name} took {serac}'s commission a hundred and thirteen years ago. The Mandate kept your rank warm. The pension office keeps it under 'missing, presumed timeless'.

intro.founder.text: {origin.name} was one of the captains who founded the Hauler Hansa. The Hansa is a hundred and thirteen years old now, and has a museum. You are in it, in a glass case marked 'presumed'.

intro.from_cargo1.text: {origin.name}, {origin.rank}, flew when the Hansa was new. That was a hundred and thirteen years ago by the dock clocks. Long sublight legs and longer sleeps kept you younger than the calendar. The calendar has not forgiven you.

intro.fresh.text: 2533. You have a captain's licence and a kit bag. The licence says captain. The hiring hall at {place} says able hand, and the hall is the one that is hiring.

opening.pod.title: The needle
text: Your first command went into the needle at Beta with a full hold. The needle shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark.

The pod kept you cold and asleep for nineteen years, until a salvager found it. The salvager claimed the pod and paid you a finder's tenth of your own scrap value: three hundred credits. Your ship did not come with you.
The needle shed you again. You know the drill by now: the file of ships, the jolt, the pod tumbling in the dark, and the long cold sleep.
The salvager who found you this time paid a finder's tenth of your own scrap value, three hundred credits, and asked if you did this on purpose. Your ship did not come with you. It never does.

The last needle you flew in 2460 shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark. As it let you go, the needle said something in needle-talk. You still remember it, and you still do not understand it.

The pod kept you cold and asleep for seventy-three years, until a salvager found it. The salvager claimed the pod and paid you a finder's tenth of your own scrap value: three hundred credits. Your ship did not come with you.
The early needles were not built for haulers of your mass. One of them shed you like a bad link: one moment the file of ships, the next a pod tumbling in the dark.

The pod kept you cold for decades, on top of the decades your long legs had already taken. The salvager who found it was a Rockwarden prospector who knew your name from the cooperative's books. She gave you three hundred credits and would not take the pod. Your ship did not come with you.

hall.first.title: The hiring hall
text: The hiring hall at {place} is a long room with a berths board at one end and the plants' shift lists at the other. Captains post what they want and what they pay. Nobody posts what they carry.

The old hands on the benches talk about people who should be dead. A loader agrobot one hand short, older than the Hansa, still works the cargo rings. A singer rides every needle and never gets older. And a man called {serac} has not aged a day since the Debacle, or since long before it.

thought.first_work.text: No ship. The berths board pays on arrival, the plants pay by the shift, and either way I learn something.

thought.find_adit.text: The old hands say the loader agrobot works the cargo rings, Beta most of all, two turns at a dock and then on. If anything on the docks remembers my century, it does. It likes people who work the ring.

thought.the_pod.text: The world moved on while I slept in the pod. First find out who is still in it, then what became of my ship.

thought.never_came_out.text: My ship never came out of the needle. Somebody who rides the needles might know where they really go.

floor.hovertank.title: The hovertank plant
floor.hovertank.text: The plant builds hovertanks for whoever pays, the Mandate this year. The foreman says the design goes back to a legion prototype that came to Delta a century ago, flipped once, and was never quite the same.

variants.text: The first drawing in the plant's lobby is the legion's prototype, the one you delivered to Delta c a century ago. Someone has written 'mind the skirt' in the margin. The line still builds it, for the Mandate this year.
The plant's licence came through {serac}'s depot a century ago, with the prototype you sold him. The foreman calls the design 'the colonel's tank' and does not know which colonel.

floor.mine.title: The deep levels
floor.mine.text: The deep levels go down eleven now. The old hands will not go below nine, and nobody says why.

variants.text: On level nine there is a plaque with twelve names, and a thirteenth line left blank 'for the hauler'. The old hands will not go below nine. Now you know why they stop there.
Far down the galleries a mining agrobot with a Rockwarden share badge is still boring the first gallery's fourth extension. {aela} does not stop to look. It never did. Next time, perhaps.

floor.biomass.title: The farm drums
floor.biomass.text: The farm drums turn all shift. The agrobots tend the crops, the people tend the agrobots, and nobody tends the people.

variants.text: When you clock in, the agrobots pass a pulse of light down the row. The Sowers kept the relay you let them keep, and it is a node now. Nodes remember.
Geod's Row grows from the seed stock you brought a century ago. The tender beside you says the first fields were 'given by a hauler', as if haulers gave things.

hands.plumb.title: {plumb}
hands.plumb.text: {plumb} checks her own manifest twice, then yours. 'I pay what the board says,' she says. 'The board says less than the others. That is how you know it is true.'

hands.ghillie.title: {ghillie}
hands.ghillie.text: {ghillie} named his ship the Low Water, he says, because that is when you find what people dropped. He does not say what he carries. He pays half again, and he does not ask what you carried either.

hands.caspic.title: {caspic}
hands.caspic.text: {caspic} has orders for everything, including you. 'Navigator, gunner or steward. The Mandate does not hire loaders. Loaders ask about crates.'

variants.text: {caspic} reads your file and salutes. Then he reads the date on it and stops saluting. 'Navigator, gunner or steward,' he says. 'Sir. Or not, sir. I will ask.'

hands.vrtoch.title: {vrtoch}
hands.vrtoch.text: The Errata is the last ring-research ship nobody impounded, because nobody could find its registration. 'We measure the Gyrotron's silence,' says {vrtoch}. 'It is a very precise silence.'

hands.caboose.title: {caboose}
hands.caboose.text: {caboose} blesses your kit bag 'in apparent good order and condition'. His papers say {caboose.full}, from his scan code; the old hands still call him Officer Deks, from before the Cargolytes relabelled him. The Clean Lading rides at the tail of every needle, where the Sender looks first. It is cold back there, the pay is low, and nobody asks your name.

friends.adit.title: {dock_loader}
text: The old loader agrobot works beside you for a whole shift without a word. At the end it corrects your grip. 'You will last,' it says. From {dock_loader.short}, that is a speech.
'I keep lists,' it says. 'Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
{dock_loader} still has the hand you brought back from Geod's Row, and the hand still says USE NO HOOKS. It knows you before you speak. 'Seventy-three years,' it says. 'I kept it oiled.'
'I keep lists now,' it says. 'Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
{dock_loader} turns its sensor head when you pass. 'Beta, 2460,' it says. 'You stacked badly then too.'
'I keep lists now. Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'
'The old manifests have your name,' says {dock_loader}. 'Your crates were always square. The loaders talked about you, the ones who trained me.'
'I keep lists. Every hull that went into the yards after the Debacle, and every name on every tag. Ask.'

choices.say: Ask who else is still alive
Work the next shift beside it

friends.adit_ship.text: {dock_loader} runs its lists, twice. 'Every hull that came out of a needle since the Debacle is in here,' it says. 'Yours went in. It never came out. Neither did the file it flew with.' It thinks about that. 'Ask {warp_singer}. She rides every needle. She would know where they go when they do not come back.'

variants.text: {dock_loader} runs its lists, twice. 'Every hull that came out of a needle since the Debacle is in here,' it says. 'Yours went in. It never came out. Neither did the file it flew with.' It thinks about that. 'You speak needle-talk. So does {warp_singer}. Ask her what the needle said to you.'

friends.adit_who.text: '{aela} still digs for the Rockwardens,' says {dock_loader}. '{neon_sleeper} sleeps at Delta between decades. {warp_singer} rides every needle and does not age. {serac} does not age either, but nobody calls him a friend. He asked about you last month.'

friends.adit_work.text: You work the next shift beside {dock_loader}. It never says a word you did not need, and by the end your grip is right. 'Now ask me something,' it says. 'Friends ask.'

ch1.title: The Hiring Hall
text: 2533. The Debacle is over, and so is everything it paid for: the research houses are broke, the ring is a joke, and the hulls that touched it sit in impound yards.
Your ship is gone, and nobody can tell you where. The hiring hall opens at the start of every shift.

ch1.friend.title: An old friend
ch1.friend.text: Find someone on the docks who remembers your century.

ch2.title: Old Friends
text: Some of the people you knew are still alive, a century and more later: machines, sleepers, the ones who rode the long legs. Find them.

ch2.friends.title: Old friends found
ch2.friends.text: Find the people who outlived their century.

ch3.title: A Bridge Again
text: Someone has found you, and they have a ship and a job that nobody else will take.
